observation:
Until these ran, every DCU campaign whose measurement could discriminate showed the authored candidate losing to its starter reference -- gelu_tanh_backward at 0.532, prelu at 0.557, gemm at 0.747 -- and the rest sat on a dispatch floor where neither arm could be told from the other. An earlier reading of this evidence said so in general terms. That reading is now wrong, and the correction is the finding.

Three campaigns confirmed a candidate faster than its baseline. per_channel_moments is the one worth attention: 0.006719 against 0.009439, a ratio of 1.405, with both arms above the floor so the comparison means something, and above the Study's declared materiality ratio of 1.05 rather than inside it. momentum_sgd and pairwise_sqdist are 1.057 and 1.054, which clear materiality narrowly. Two more are faster and do not clear it -- gelu_tanh at 1.026 and swiglu at 1.029 -- and are excluded here rather than folded in, because a ratio inside the declared materiality is what that declaration exists to call indistinguishable. Five candidates are nominally ahead; three are ahead by enough to say so.

One more run would make it four, and it is excluded rather than counted. gelu_tanh qualified a second time and that run reads 0.005439 against 0.006399, a ratio of 1.176 above materiality. Its candidate sits exactly on the dispatch floor, so the assay has stopped resolving the arm the ratio is about: the number says the baseline costs more than the floor, which was already known. Counting it would be counting the timer. The three above are the ones with both arms above the floor, and that is the property that makes a ratio mean something here.

What this is and is not. It is candidate against fixed baseline inside one task, case, target and assay, under a claim scope of artifact_optimization_only -- not an arm comparison, and not a speedup against any external reference. The baseline is the starter the task ships with, so 1.405 says the author found something better than a naive reference, not that it approached what the hardware can do; nothing here measures that. Three results out of twenty-seven qualified campaigns is also a small number to generalise from, and two of the three clear materiality by less than a tenth.

The stamp on this record has now been wrong twice, and the second time was inside the correction of the first. It named f91a862a; that was moved back to 2e901f53 with the sentence 'the commit these campaigns ran at', which was false -- 2e901f53 is 08:10 on 2026-09-18 and all three campaigns had finished by 06:09. Their evidence records what they actually ran at: momentum_sgd at 0970a36e, per_channel_moments and pairwise_sqdist at 4278caf2. Both errors have the same cause as the count errors above -- a field edited to look right rather than read off the evidence -- and the fix is the same one: the revision is recorded per campaign in the medians file and checked against this field by tests/contracts/test_dcu_medians_counts.py, so the stamp cannot drift from the runs again.
proposed_change:
Nothing to change. This is recorded because the negative reading it corrects was written down first, and because it is the only evidence so far that the loop on this target produces improvement rather than parity or regression.

What would make it more than an anecdote: the shapes that produce it. All three sit above the dispatch floor, and F-2026-09-18-002 shows the floor is where most of these tasks run at the default footprint -- so a sweep at a footprint above the floor would say whether 1.405 is a property of per_channel_moments or of finally being able to measure. That is the same experiment F-2026-09-18-002 already proposes, and this record is a second reason to run it.
